messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the last kernel+driver rollout in us-west-2 we saw ~8% of A100 nodes fail to initialize NVML, escalated to incident. dmesg shows: 

maya: ```
[drm] failed to load nvidia_uvm: -22
NVRM: Xid (0000:3B:00): 79, pid=0, 0x00000000
```

raj: ugh. which combination caused it? kernel version + driver?

maya: nodes were on kernel 6.6.10 + nvidia-driver 535.86.10 + CUDA 12.1 stacks. The reproduce rate is low but consistent on certain AMIs.

simon: sounds like a kernel ABI regression w/ 6.6.10. H100 fleet in eu-west-1 unaffected (they're on 6.1.x).

elena: Confirmed. Canary pool (small us-west-2 group) hit the failure. We auto-rolled drivers via image-bake pipeline yesterday.

charlie: Incident bot: triggered auto-rollback on 3 instances, patched others to boot with blacklist nvidia_uvm hook.

deploy-bot: rollback: image bake 2026-03-17T03:14 -> reverted to bake 2026-03-14T22:08 by @charlie

raj: We need a hotfix strategy: pin driver packages on fleets where kernel is >=6.6 until we validate full compatibility. Also a gate so image-bakes don't auto-push driver upgrades for kernels we haven't validated.

maya: Agreed. Short-term proposal: 1) apt/dpkg hold OR rpm versionlock the nvidia-driver package on affected AMIs 2) add a baked-in compat-matrix file to images 3) block automated driver-bumps via CI gate if kernel version matches any known-bad entries.

simon: For Debian/Ubuntu AMIs: `apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535` is the simplest. For RHEL/CentOS: `yum install yum-plugin-versionlock` + `yum versionlock add nvidia-driver-535-*`

elena: We should be specific about package ids to avoid accidental holds of future builds. e.g. `apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535=535.86.10-0ubuntu1` or `yum versionlock add nvidia-driver-535-535.86.10*`

charlie: Also add a DKMS fallback removal step in the image bootstrap to prevent incompatible kernel module builds. Current images build modules on boot which seems to trigger the crash.

maya: Medium-term: create a lockstep compatibility matrix repo (json file) that maps kernel minor versions -> approved driver versions -> approved CUDA toolkits -> regions/fleet-tags. Bake that into images at bake-time and have the bake pipeline consult it.

raj: We can model the matrix as rows like `kernel:6.6.x -> drivers:[535.86.10] -> status:blocked` and have pipeline return non-zero if image wants to install a driver not allowed for that kernel.

simon: Quick ops runbook for this incident copy into /runbooks/kernel-driver-compat: commands to hold, to force repro, to revert AMI: 

simon: ```
# pin debian/ubuntu package
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535=535.86.10-0ubuntu1
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535

# pin rpm (rhel/centos)
sudo yum install -y yum-plugin-versionlock
sudo yum versionlock add nvidia-driver-535-535.86.10*

# rollback AMI (example)
aws ec2 create-image --instance-id i-abcdef --name "bake-revert-2026-03-14"
```

elena: I'll push a temp CI gate: any image-bake that updates `nvidia-driver*` will fail if `kernel_release` in image metadata starts with `6.6`. PR inbound.

maya: For safety, we should also annotate the fleet-state in the console: add a flag `driver_pinned:true` with reason and pinned-version so SRE can quickly see which pools are pinned.

charlie: Ops action list I can take now: 1) run apt-mark hold on all us-west-2 canaries (in progress) 2) add versionlock rules to rhel h100 pool 3) disable auto-driver-bump in bake pipeline (temp)

raj: Who owns the compat matrix design? I'll volunteer with simon and elena to draft schema and gating logic.

maya: 👍 Also consider adding a gradual canary policy: driver-bump job should only target a tiny canary subset, wait 24h, then expand. If any kernel-driver regressions are added to our internal tracker, chef/packer/bake pipeline should consult the matrix and abort.

elena: PR for gate is up: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/image-bake/pulls/742 — it enforces `kernel->driver` restrictions via a small python check.

charlie: I'm running a fleet audit now to list all nodes with kernel >=6.6 + driver 535.* and will post counts in 10m.

maya: Postmortem notes: we need clearer ownership for image-bakes (who approves driver bumps), add an automated smoke test that loads NVML on boot, and record the exact failing stacktrace in the kernel-driver tickets.

raj: For the hotfix release notes: outline pinned versions, regions affected (us-west-2), rollback AMIs used, and the bake gate. I'll draft and send to support+customers impacted.

ops-bot: audit-report: 42 nodes matching kernel>=6.6 + nvidia-driver=535.86.10 — 28 in us-west-2, 14 in us-east-1 (old AMIs)

maya: Good catch. Let's coordinate the staged unpin only after we validate across kernels 6.6.x, 6.5.x, and 6.1.x on a small A/B test. Assignments: charlie (run audit + holds), elena (gate PR), simon (run smoke tests), raj/maya (compat matrix). I'll follow up in #incidents with the final hotfix summary. :thumbsup:
